#### New Kenosha hub significantly expands G10 Fulfillment’s Midwest warehouse capacity

 Posted in Kenosha County Economic Development 

A Delavan-based third-party logistics and fulfillment company has significantly expanded its Midwest warehouse capacity after moving into a new distribution facility in Kenosha.

G10 Fulfillment now occupies 315,000 square feet of a 600,000-square-foot building at 12345 38th St., just off Interstate 94. The move increases G10’s dock capacity to 65 doors from 30.

“The Midwest is probably the most important hub for us,” said co-founder and CEO Mark Becker, who was on hand Thursday for a ribbon-cutting at the facility. He pointed to the region’s freight infrastructure and its location along the trucking corridor between Chicago and Milwaukee.

Becker said the facility can handle nearly 7 acres of inventory under one roof. G10 shares the building with food manufacturer Eagle Foods.

G10 invested about $2 million in the Kenosha buildout, which Becker said covered racking, automation and staffing costs.

results.author: Nick Sloan
results.text:
Wagner Logistics expansion to bring 80 jobs to Liberty - KMBC

# Wagner Logistics expanding in Liberty, bringing nearly 80 new jobs

Updated: 8:06 PM CDT Oct 14, 2026

Nick Sloan Digital Content Producer

Updated: 8:06 PM CDT Oct 14, 2026

Nick Sloan Digital Content Producer

LIBERTY, Mo. —

A logistics company is expanding its operations in Liberty, bringing nearly 80 new jobs to the area.

The city announced Wednesday that Wagner Logistics will lease two warehouse facilities in the Liberty area totaling more than 830,000 square feet.

The company will provide warehouse operations, distribution services and transportation management, helping manufacturers move products from production facilities to their next destinations.

"The City of Liberty is committed to fostering a vibrant economic development environment and we are excited to welcome Wagner Logistics to Liberty,” Mayor Greg Canuteson said in a statement.

The mayor said the expansion will help bring more jobs to the community while strengthening the city's tax base. 

The city did not provide a timeline for when the new jobs will be filled.

Logistics Plus Signs 744K-SF Wilmer Warehouse Lease - Connect CRE

 

 By: Mike Boyd 

# Logistics Plus Signs 744K-SF Wilmer Warehouse Lease 

Logistics Plus has signed a 744,452-square-foot industrial lease in the southern Dallas suburb of Wilmer. The Pennsylvania-based provider of freight and fulfillment services will occupy the entire Building 2 within the Southport Logistics Center, an approximately 1.5 million-square-foot development. Building 2 features 123 dock doors, three drive-in doors and 4,647 square feet of speculative office space. Building 1, still vacant, includes 121 dock doors, four drive-in doors, 389 car parking spaces, 170 trailer parking spaces, and 3,534 square feet of speculative office space. 

Kurt Griffin and Nathan Orbin of JLL represented the landlord, a joint venture between Bandera Ventures and Invesco Real Estate, in the lease negotiations.

In addition to the Wilmer site, Logistics Plus has another warehouse in Haslet. The facilities have a combined 2 million square feet of storage space in the region.

Logistics Plus has over 12 million square feet of commercial warehouse space across North America.

# Logistics Newcomer Secures Its First South Florida Foothold 

October 14, 2026/ in Industrial / Flex, Industry News, Miami-Dade County Industrial / Flex, NA / by CRE-sources Editorial Staff / 

Cargo Lift Solutions has leased 37,000 square feet at Prologis Palmetto Tradeport, located at 8090 NW 77th Court in Medley, for its first facility. The air cargo logistics company signed a five-year agreement with landlord Prologis and occupied the industrial space in September 2026. Financial terms were not disclosed.

Fausto Commercial’s Kodiak Fields and Ben Kunzle represented the tenant. JLL’s Ana Rivera represented Prologis.

The space offers 24-foot clear heights, 12 dock doors and one drive-in door. Airport proximity and highway access position the facility to connect air freight with truck distribution.

The commitment comes as Miami-Dade industrial vacancy declined to 6.5% in the third quarter, according to Colliers.
